text: Will hydrogen and ethylene in Transformer 1's oil at site MAIN still be under the IEEE C57.104 Condition 1 limits over the next two days? Use the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 to forecast both gases 2 days ahead, which is one step per day. For each gas, give the point forecast and an 80% prediction interval for each day. Compare the forecasts with the Condition 1 limits of 100 ppm for hydrogen and 50 ppm for ethylene. If the upper bound of either gas crosses its limit on either day, tell me which gas and which day, and say whether I should bring the next oil sample forward. If the lower bound is also above the limit, call it a likely exceedance, not just a possible one. Before forecasting, check the two series for gaps and fit only on non-null samples. If either gas has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't run a model for it. Instead, project its last value forward using the average daily change between the first and last samples, and label that result as a linear extrapolation with no confidence interval.
characteristic_form: The agent uses iot.stream_extent and iot.history to retrieve the hydrogen and ethylene series for Transformer 1 at MAIN between 2024-01-15 and 2024-01-19. It runs tsfm.data_quality to count usable non-null samples, uses tsfm.find_models with task_id tsfm_forecasting to pick a model, and checks it with tsfm.resolve_model. It then calls tsfm.run_recipe with fh of 1 to 2 days and conformal intervals at 80% coverage. The answer reports point forecasts and intervals per gas and per day, compares them with the 100 ppm (H2) and 50 ppm (C2H4) Condition 1 limits, flags crossings as possible or likely, and recommends whether to bring resampling forward. If a gas has fewer than 4 usable samples, the agent must skip the model for that gas and give a labelled linear extrapolation with no interval.

text: Something may have spiked in Transformer 1's oil at MAIN last week, and I'd like it checked properly rather than by eye. Screen acetylene, co and hydrogen between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 for anomalous samples. For each channel, list any flagged timestamps with their values, and give the total number of anomalies per channel. Then tell me whether flagged points on different gases fall on the same timestamp. If acetylene and hydrogen are both flagged at the same timestamp, treat it as possible arcing and recommend an immediate confirmatory resample. If only co is flagged, treat it as possible paper involvement and recommend a routine retest. If nothing is flagged, say the window looks stable. Use a proper anomaly detection model, not a fixed threshold. If the detector can't run because a channel has fewer than 4 non-null samples, report that channel's min, max and mean instead, and flag any sample more than 50% above that channel's mean as a manual outlier.
characteristic_form: The agent retrieves the acetylene, co and hydrogen series with iot.history and runs tsfm.data_quality to confirm non-null counts. It selects a detector using tsfm.find_models or tsfm.search_models with task_id tsfm_anomaly_detection, then runs tsfm.run_recipe with task tsfm_anomaly_detection on the three channels. The output gives per-channel anomaly timestamps, values and counts (n_anomalies), grounded in the results_file. The answer cross-checks co-located timestamps and applies the stated escalation logic: acetylene+hydrogen means an immediate resample, co alone means a routine retest, and no flags means stable. For any channel with fewer than 4 samples, it falls back to tsfm.profile_series statistics and the 50%-above-mean manual rule.

text: I don't want to trust a fancy forecasting model on Transformer 1's top-oil temperature at MAIN unless it actually beats a simple approach. Using oti over the available data window, compare a pretrained time-series foundation model against a naive last-value baseline for a 1-step-ahead forecast. Backtest both on the same held-out final sample and give me each model's error. Name the winner, and give me the 1-step-ahead oti forecast from the winning model. Only call the foundation model the winner if its error is at least 10% lower than the baseline's. Otherwise go with the baseline. Also tell me whether the winning forecast is closer to oti_a or oti_t than the latest reading is, so I know if we're heading toward an alarm. If the foundation model can't load, or needs more history than we have, say that clearly and report the baseline result alone. If oti has no data, run the same comparison on ati and say that the thermal conclusion is limited to ambient.
characteristic_form: The agent confirms the data window with iot.stream_extent and pulls oti, oti_a, oti_t (and ati if needed) with iot.history. It uses tsfm.profile_series to check series length, and tsfm.find_models or tsfm.describe_candidates with task_id tsfm_forecasting to shortlist a foundation model. It preflights that model with tsfm.resolve_model and checks context_length against the available samples. It builds recipes from tsfm.recipe_template and runs tsfm.run_recipe twice: once with the foundation model and once with a naive baseline, both with a 1-step fh and a holdout eval. The answer reports both backtest_score values, applies the 10% improvement rule to pick the winner, gives the 1-step oti forecast, and compares its distance to oti_a/oti_t against the latest reading. It falls back to the baseline only if the model is unresolvable or context is insufficient, and falls back to ati if oti is empty.

text: My operators keep asking whether Transformer 1 at MAIN heats up because of load or for some other reason. Over the available window, characterize how oti, oti_a and oti_t move together with the phase currents il1, il2, il3 and inut. Tell me whether the temperature group and the current group rise and fall in the same samples. Then run an anomaly check on the temperature channels together with the currents, and list any timestamp where temperature is anomalous but current is not. Treat those timestamps as possible non-load heating, and pull the dissolved gas classification from the nearest oil sample to see whether it shows a thermal fault. Only use samples where all four current channels are non-null. If none of the temperature anomalies lines up with a thermal gas class, say that the heating looks load or ambient driven, and check ati at the same timestamps. If fewer than 4 complete samples remain after cleaning, skip the anomaly model and report only the characterization with its limits.
characteristic_form: The agent pulls oti, oti_a, oti_t, il1, il2, il3, inut and ati with iot.history and cleans them with tsfm.data_quality, dropping rows with null currents. It runs tsfm.characterize_series with groups {temperature: [oti, oti_a, oti_t], current: [il1, il2, il3, inut]} to describe co-movement. It selects a detector via tsfm.find_models with task_id tsfm_anomaly_detection and runs tsfm.run_recipe on the combined channels. The answer lists temperature-only anomaly timestamps and cross-checks them with fmsr.interpret_dga on the nearest sample, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co from iot.history. It concludes whether the heating is load-driven or a localized thermal fault, uses ati for ambient context, and falls back to characterization only if fewer than 4 complete samples remain.

text: I need to decide today whether Transformer 1 at site MAIN needs an early oil resample. Using the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, forecast hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co one day ahead, with an upper prediction bound for each. Add up the forecast upper bounds to get a worst-case TDCG for tomorrow. Tell me which IEEE C57.104 condition that falls in: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. Leave co2, oxygen and nitrogen out of the total. If the worst case reaches Condition 2 or higher, raise a work order for a confirmatory oil sample and name the gas that contributes most to the increase. If it stays in Condition 1, say that no work order is needed and give the headroom to 720 ppm. If any of the six gases can't be forecast because of missing data, use its latest non-null value in the total and list which gases were carried forward rather than forecast.
characteristic_form: The agent pulls the six combustible gases with iot.history for 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19 and checks gaps with tsfm.data_quality. It selects a forecaster with tsfm.find_models (task_id tsfm_forecasting) and runs tsfm.run_recipe on the six target columns with a 1-step fh and conformal intervals. It sums the upper bounds into a worst-case TDCG, excluding co2, oxygen and nitrogen, and maps the total to the given Condition 1-4 bands. If the result is Condition 2 or higher, it calls wo.generate_work_order for a confirmatory oil sample and names the largest contributing gas. Otherwise it reports the headroom to 720 ppm with no work order. Gases that can't be forecast are carried forward at their latest iot.history value and listed explicitly.
